note: A failed asset export now says why: `assetSummary.unavailable[]`, `failures[]` and the asset manifest carry `errorDetail` (the step, the time it took and what Figma or the transport said), where the plugin used to swallow the exception and leave only `DEVUP_ASSET_EXPORT_FAILED`; rebuild the plugin bundle to get it. Failures the plugin itself answered come back over the bridge in the remote `use_figma` shape, so they are classified as on the remote path (a missing node is `DEVUP_FIGMA_NODE_NOT_FOUND`, -32602) instead of all reading `DEVUP_FIGMA_DIRECT_UNAVAILABLE`; a host relays the distinction with `scriptError`. That had made Figma's runtime saying "Unable to establish connection to Figma after 10 seconds" - which it answered to every read of data it had not loaded (layers inside instances, other pages, variables and styles) while the file's tab sat behind another file's tab in the desktop app - look like a direct-path outage; the error and the asset failure now say to click the file's tab, and `completenessReport.resources` carries what the variable and style lookups threw (`lookupError`) with the same `hint`, where 37 tokens lost that way used to read like 37 that do not exist. `widthBehavior` marks roots drawn narrower than any screen (320px) `componentSized` and leaves out their `consumer-policy-required` findings (`summary.componentRootSuppressed`). `devup_runtime_audit` ingest returns `visualComparisons`, a ready `devup_visual_compare` call per screenshot taken at a drawn width with what the audit verified filled in and the rest named, and `devup_visual_compare` pins a reference given by `artifactId` itself (`environment.filledByServer`). Codegen no longer re-scans the source map per source-map entry when auditing generated attributes: a 790-node, three-width screen projects in 0.58 s instead of 15.3 s, with byte-identical output.
